title: Regular multiplicativity defect and cochain correction across a square-zero ideal
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $J\subseteq A$ an ideal with $J^2=0$, $A_0=A/J$, $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A_0$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $H=\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $G$ be affine group schemes over $S$, with multiplication, inverse and identity satisfying the group diagrams. Assume that $C$ is flat as an $A$-module (tensoring with $C$ preserves injections), and that $G\to S$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $H_0=H\times_SS_0$, $G_0=G\times_SS_0$ [def-pc-base-change], and $C_0=C/JC$. Let $u_0:H_0\to G_0$ be an $S_0$-group homomorphism and let $f:H\to G$ be an $S$-scheme morphism reducing to $u_0$; $f$ need not preserve identity or multiplication. Let $P=e_0^*\Omega^1_{G_0/S_0}$ be the cotangent $A_0$-module at the identity: its homomorphisms to a module $N$ are the $A_0$-derivations of the coordinate ring of $G_0$ to $N$, where that ring acts through its identity augmentation. Set $L=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0}(P,A_0)$ and $E=L\otimes_{A_0}J$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Conjugation in $G_0$, differentiated at its identity and composed with $u_0$, makes $E$ an $H_0$-module; equivalently it gives an $A_0$-linear coaction $E\to E\otimes_{A_0}C_0$ satisfying the coproduct and counit identities.
For every flat commutative $A$-algebra $R$, put $R_0=R/JR$. There is an additive-group isomorphism
$$\kappa_R:E\otimes_{A_0}R_0\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(G(R)\to G_0(R_0)),$$
natural in flat $A$-algebras $R$. On the right the group law is multiplication. Conjugating $\kappa_R(v)$ by $f(h)$ corresponds to the action of the reduction of $h\in H(R)$ on $v$ through the displayed $H_0$-coaction.
For $n\geq1$ define the module of regular $n$-cochains by $C^n(H_0,E)=E\otimes_{A_0}C_0^{\otimes n}$. Evaluation at $h_1,\ldots,h_n\in H_0(B)$ for an $A_0$-algebra $B$ uses their algebra maps $C_0\to B$ and multiplication in $B$. There is a unique $c_f\in C^2(H_0,E)$ characterized on the universal pair of $H$-points, over the flat algebra $C\otimes_A C$, by
$$\kappa(c_f(h,k))=f(hk)f(k)^{-1}f(h)^{-1}.$$
It satisfies the regular cocycle identity
$$h\mathbin{\cdot}c_f(k,l)-c_f(hk,l)+c_f(h,kl)-c_f(h,k)=0\quad\text{in }C^3(H_0,E).$$
For every regular $1$-cochain $b\in E\otimes_{A_0}C_0$, its image under $\kappa_C$ defines an $S$-scheme morphism $\widetilde b:H\to G$ reducing to the identity section. The morphism $f_b(h)=\widetilde b(h)f(h)$ reduces to $u_0$ and has defect
$$c_{f_b}(h,k)=c_f(h,k)-\bigl(h\mathbin{\cdot}b(k)-b(hk)+b(h)\bigr).$$
Vanishing of $c_f$ is equivalent to the equality of scheme morphisms $f\circ m_H=m_G\circ(f\times f)$.

source.place: Conrad, Reductive group schemes (2014), Proposition B.2.5, printed pp.286-287, explicit defect and correction formulas; proof of Corollary B.2.6, printed p.287, identification of the square-zero kernel and its adjoint action. Flat test algebras suffice here; no claim identifying the kernel on arbitrary non-flat test algebras is made. Online source read; WANTED local archive literature/conrad-reductive-group-schemes.pdf.

proof.text: Write $G=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with augmentation $\varepsilon:B\to A$. The smooth-differentials theorem [lem-ag-smooth-relative-differentials-finite-locally-free] makes $\Omega^1_{G/S}$ finite locally free. Pulling a local free frame back along $e_0:S_0\to G$ gives a local free frame of $e_0^*\Omega^1_{G/S}$, directly from the tensor-pullback definition [def-pc-module-pullback]. By differential base change [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] this is $e_0^*\Omega^1_{G_0/S_0}$. Thus its module of sections is the module $P$ in the statement. Apply [lem-pc-finite-flat-affine-sections-projective] to this finite locally free sheaf on the affine scheme $S_0$, with its entire affine open: $P$ is finitely presented and projective. Neither constant rank nor Noetherianity is needed.

source.place: Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change); finite projective affine sections as in the cited node.

proof.text: Choose finite generators of $P$ from its finite presentation. Projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] splits the resulting surjection $A_0^r\to P$. Writing the splitting in coordinates gives $p_i\in P$ and $\phi_i\in L$ with $p=\sum_i\phi_i(p)p_i$. For any $A_0$-module $N$, the map $L\otimes N\to\operatorname{Hom}(P,N)$, $\phi\otimes n\mapsto(p\mapsto\phi(p)n)$, has inverse $t\mapsto\sum_i\phi_i\otimes t(p_i)$: the two composites are identities by the displayed dual-basis equation, also applied to functionals. These maps commute with every map of coefficient modules, since their formulas do. This is an elementary dual-basis calculation, including $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective), splitting of a free surjection; explicit finite dual-basis calculation.

proof.text: For a flat $A$-algebra $R$, tensoring the injection $J\hookrightarrow A$ with $R$ is injective, by the stated meaning of flatness (also [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection]). Its image is exactly $JR$, so $J\otimes_A R\cong JR$. Since $J^2=0$, balancing gives $J\otimes_A R=J\otimes_{A_0}R_0$: the maps send $j\otimes r$ to $j\otimes\bar r$ and back, the latter independent of the lift because $J(JR)=0$. In particular $(JR)^2=0$. For $R_n=C^{\otimes_A n}$, the tensor functor is the composite of $n$ tensor functors with $C$, so it preserves injections and $R_n$ is flat. Sending each tensor factor to its quotient gives $R_n/JR_n\cong C_0^{\otimes_{A_0}n}$; an inverse sends a tensor of residue classes to the residue class of the tensor of any lifts, which is well-defined by multilinearity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-group-space-square-zero-kernel-module] to $G/S$ and $\operatorname{Spec}R_0\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}R$, whose ideal is $JR$. Its conclusion identifies the kernel, additively, with homomorphisms from the pulled-back cotangent sheaf to $\widetilde{JR}$. The affine-chart clause of [lem-sfb-space-affine-module-correspondence] identifies these with $\operatorname{Hom}_{R_0}(R_0\otimes_{A_0}P,JR)=\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0}(P,JR)$; the equality sends a map $t$ to $p\mapsto t(1\otimes p)$, with inverse $r\otimes p\mapsto rt(p)$. Steps 2 and 3 identify this module with $L\otimes J\otimes R_0=E\otimes R_0$. Define $\kappa_R$ as the resulting inverse kernel identification. To check naturality, use the difference description in [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization]: the corresponding point has coordinate map $\varepsilon_R+D$, where $D:B\to JR$ is the derivation associated to $P\to JR$. A map $R\to R'$ sends it to $\varepsilon_{R'}+D'$ by composition. This is exactly the coefficient map in steps 2 and 3, proving the claimed naturality.

proof.text: Here is the regular adjoint action, with no choice of a lift. Put $B_0=B/JB$. Over $B_0$, take the universal point $g\in G_0(B_0)$ and the automorphism $x\mapsto gxg^{-1}$ of $(G_0)_{B_0}$, fixing its identity. Pullback of derivations along its coordinate map induces a $B_0$-linear endomorphism of the cotangent module $B_0\otimes P$, by the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. This is the cotangent transpose of the linear postcomposition map of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization], applied to the identity lift over a square-zero extension of $B_0$. Its transpose acts on $\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0}(P,B_0)=L\otimes B_0$ using step 2. Evaluating on $\phi\otimes1$ defines $L\to L\otimes B_0$. This is a coaction: evaluating the two iterated maps on the universal pair gives the equality of derivatives of $x\mapsto g(hxh^{-1})g^{-1}$ and $x\mapsto(gh)x(gh)^{-1}$; evaluation at the identity gives the identity map. Both equalities hold on every generator $\mathrm db$ by substitution in the coordinate maps, hence on the entire cotangent module. Tensor this action with $J$, on which the group acts trivially, and substitute $u_0$ in the universal $g$. This defines the asserted $A_0$-linear $H_0$-coaction on $E$.

proof.text: We check that this action is the actual conjugation action on the kernel. Let $g\in G(R)$ and let a kernel point have coordinate map $\varepsilon_R+D$, as in step 4. Write $\Delta^{(2)}(a)=\sum a_1\otimes a_2\otimes a_3$ for the iterated coproduct of $B$. Substitution in the three factors shows that the difference of the coordinate map of $g\kappa_R(v)g^{-1}$ from $\varepsilon_R$ is $$a\longmapsto\sum g^*(a_1)D(a_2)(g^{-1})^*(a_3).$$ The terms with $\varepsilon_R$ in the middle sum to $\varepsilon_R(a)$ by the group inverse identity. Because each $D(a_2)$ belongs to $JR$ and $(JR)^2=0$, each other factor in this formula may be replaced by its reduction modulo $JR$. Thus this is precisely the derivative of conjugation by $g_0$, as constructed in step 5, acting on the coefficient derivation. Equivalently it is the linear postcomposition map of [lem-sfb-space-square-zero-lift-linearization]. For $g=f(h)$ its reduction is $u_0(h_0)$, which proves the claimed equivariance of $\kappa_R$.

proof.text: By the tensor universal property, algebra maps $C\otimes_A C\to R$ are exactly pairs of algebra maps $C\to R$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and the affine-spectrum correspondence identify $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_A C)$ with $H\times_SH$. Over the flat algebra $R_2=C\otimes_A C$, let $h,k$ be the two universal $H$-points and set $d(h,k)=f(hk)f(k)^{-1}f(h)^{-1}$. Its reduction is $u_0(h_0k_0)u_0(k_0)^{-1}u_0(h_0)^{-1}=1$, so $d(h,k)$ is in the kernel. Define $c_f=\kappa_{R_2}^{-1}(d(h,k))$, viewed by step 3 as an element of $E\otimes C_0\otimes C_0$. This is the claimed regular cochain, uniquely determined because $\kappa_{R_2}$ is bijective. Every pair of $H$-points over a flat $A$-algebra comes from a unique algebra map $R_2\to R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Naturality of $\kappa$ therefore gives the displayed defect formula on all such pairs. More generally, substitution of coordinate maps in any $A_0$-algebra is the cochain evaluation specified in the statement; it makes sense without lifting those points.

proof.text: Work over $R_3=C\otimes_A C\otimes_A C$ with its universal triple. The defining equation is $f(hk)=d(h,k)f(h)f(k)$. Compute $f((hk)l)=f(h(kl))$ using this equation twice on either side, then cancel $f(h)f(k)f(l)$ on the right. The result is $$d(hk,l)d(h,k)=d(h,kl)\bigl(f(h)d(k,l)f(h)^{-1}\bigr).$$ All four factors lie in the abelian kernel identified in step 4. Applying its additive identification and the conjugation formula of step 6 gives $c_f(hk,l)+c_f(h,k)=c_f(h,kl)+h\cdot c_f(k,l)$. Rearranging proves the stated cocycle identity in $E\otimes C_0^{\otimes3}$, because the triple is universal. This calculation uses no normalization at the identity.

proof.text: For $b\in E\otimes C_0$, the point $\kappa_C(b)\in G(C)$ is exactly an $S$-morphism $\widetilde b:H\to G$, by the affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Its reduction is the identity morphism $H_0\to S_0\to G_0$ because it belongs to the kernel. Multiply it with $f$ using the group-scheme multiplication to obtain $f_b$. Its reduction is $1\,u_0=u_0$. After pulling back along any of the coordinate maps $C\to R_n$, naturality in step 4 identifies its value with $\kappa_{R_n}$ of the corresponding evaluation of $b$. Thus the construction produces scheme morphisms and the required regular evaluations.

proof.text: In the universal pair algebra write $\beta(h)=\widetilde b(h)$. Expanding the defect of $f_b$ and regrouping adjacent inverse factors gives $$d_b(h,k)=\beta(hk)d(h,k)\bigl(f(h)\beta(k)^{-1}f(h)^{-1}\bigr)\beta(h)^{-1}.$$ Each factor on the right is in the abelian kernel. The additive identification of step 4 and equivariance of step 6 therefore give $$c_{f_b}(h,k)=b(hk)+c_f(h,k)-h\cdot b(k)-b(h).$$ This is the stated formula with its minus sign. Since the pair is universal, it is an equality in the regular cochain module, not merely an identity on some residue-field points.

proof.text: The equality $c_f=0$ is equivalent through $\kappa_{R_2}$ to $d(h,k)=1$ at the universal pair, hence by right multiplication to $f(hk)=f(h)f(k)$ there. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum], equality of the coordinate maps $B\to C\otimes_A C$ is exactly equality of the two $S$-morphisms $H\times_SH\to G$. This proves both implications of the last assertion. It also explains why all preceding universal-point calculations are identities of regular cochains, with no assumption that points over fields detect equality.
